title: Indoor Unit External Protection Device Activated
shortDescription: An external safety device connected to the indoor unit has tripped.
fullDescription:
The A0 error indicates that an external protection device wired to the indoor unit has activated, interrupting normal operation. This is commonly a drain pan float switch, external thermostat, or auxiliary safety device.

The indoor PCB senses the open circuit on the external input terminals and shuts the unit down to prevent damage such as water overflow or overheating. The error remains until the tripped device resets and the circuit is restored.

Technicians must identify which external device triggered, correct the underlying condition (e.g., clear the drain pan), and verify wiring integrity before restarting the system.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before inspecting wiring or the drain system.

causes.cause: Drain pan float switch tripped due to clogged condensate line
External thermostat or interlock circuit open
Loose or damaged wiring on external protection terminals

symptoms: A0 displayed on remote or wired controller

fixSteps.title: Power off at breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power to both indoor and outdoor units for safety.

fixSteps.title: Inspect condensate drain
fixSteps.instruction: Check for clogged drain line or full drain pan. Clear any blockage with wet/dry vac.

fixSteps.title: Verify float switch
fixSteps.instruction: Test float switch continuity; replace if stuck or faulty.

fixSteps.title: Inspect external wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check terminal block for loose or corroded connections on T1/T2 external input.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the drain system is clear but the error persists, or if wiring inspection is needed.

faq.q: What is the most common cause of A0?
faq.a: A clogged condensate drain line triggering the float switch.

faq.q: Can I bypass the float switch?
faq.a: No. Bypassing it risks water damage to ceilings and electronics.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Lock
shortDescription: The indoor fan motor has seized or lost position feedback.
fullDescription:
A2 indicates the indoor fan motor is locked or that position feedback from the Hall sensor has been lost. This is distinct from A6 - A2 is specifically a lock detection at startup.

Debris in the blower wheel, seized bearings, or a failed Hall sensor are common causes. The unit halts to prevent motor winding damage.

Clean the blower cage and verify free rotation before testing electrical components.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power and verify blades have stopped before handling.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blower wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Remove obstructions and verify free spin by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM motor if bearing is seized.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if motor replacement is required.

faq.a: Most modern fan motors are sealed and non-serviceable.

title: Indoor Heat Exchanger Temperature Abnormal
shortDescription: Indoor coil temperature is outside the expected operating window.
fullDescription:
Error A4 indicates the indoor heat exchanger temperature is reading outside normal bounds, typically due to low refrigerant charge, a stuck EXV, or a thermistor calibration issue.

The system disables compressor operation to prevent damage. Diagnosis requires pressure/temperature analysis by a certified tech.
safetyWarning: EPA 608 required for refrigerant work.

fixSteps.title: Test EXV
fixSteps.instruction: Pro to cycle EXV and verify response.

faq.a: No. Find and repair the leak first, per EPA rules.

title: Indoor Unit AC Input Overcurrent
shortDescription: The indoor unit drew excessive current on its AC input.
fullDescription:
Error A8 indicates indoor unit current exceeded a safe threshold. This could be caused by a shorted fan motor, failing transformer, or a damaged PCB component drawing excess current.

Inspect for burnt or blackened components and verify motor resistance before restoring power.
safetyWarning: Potential fire hazard. Do not reset repeatedly.

fixSteps.title: Visual inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burnt components or damaged insulation.

faq.a: No - repeated overcurrent events can cause fire.

title: Indoor Unit Heater Overload
shortDescription: Auxiliary electric heater strip has triggered overload protection.
fullDescription:
Error AA occurs on models equipped with an auxiliary electric strip heater when the heater overload thermal switch trips. Causes include low airflow, blocked filters, or a failed heater contactor stuck closed.

Clear airflow obstructions first; most AA events resolve with filter cleaning.
safetyWarning: Heater elements retain heat. Let cool before servicing.

fixSteps.title: Verify blower
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure fan runs on all speeds.

fixSteps.title: Test thermal limit
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity of thermal limit switch.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if thermal limit or contactor replacement needed.

faq.q: Does my unit have strip heat?
faq.a: Check nameplate - only ducted/cassette models in cold climates.

title: Sensor System Error
shortDescription: A sensor circuit on the indoor PCB reports invalid reference voltage.
fullDescription:
Error C0 indicates an internal sensor reference voltage fault. The indoor PCB cannot reliably read thermistor inputs because its analog front-end has failed.

This typically requires PCB replacement. Verify all thermistor plugs are seated before replacing.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before PCB service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistors
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug one at a time to find shorted sensor.

faq.a: Relatively rare; indicates PCB failure.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor humidity sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
Error CC indicates the indoor unit humidity sensor is reporting invalid values. This sensor is used on models with dehumidification control for precise humidity regulation.

If the unit does not have advanced dehum features, the error may have minimal operational impact but still blocks certain modes.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before opening indoor unit.
whenToCallPro: Call pro if sensor location is difficult.

faq.a: Unit may still cool, but dehum precision is lost.

title: Compressor Startup Failure
shortDescription: The compressor failed to start or lost synchronization.
fullDescription:
Error E6 indicates the inverter PCB could not successfully start the compressor or lost position feedback during operation. This may stem from a locked rotor, weak capacitor, failed IPM (intelligent power module), or faulty compressor windings.

Diagnosing E6 requires measuring winding resistance, inspecting power components, and sometimes a megger test on compressor to ground.
safetyWarning: Lethal voltages present in IPM and capacitor circuits.
symptoms: Compressor hums but does not start

fixSteps.title: Check line voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify supply voltage within 10% of nameplate.

fixSteps.title: Measure compressor windings
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance between phases should be balanced; no short to ground.

fixSteps.title: Inspect IPM module
fixSteps.instruction: Pro to test for shorted transistors.

fixSteps.title: Replace faulty component
fixSteps.instruction: PCB or compressor replacement as required.

whenToCallPro: E6 diagnosis and repair require a licensed HVAC professional.

faq.a: Depends on age; over 10 years, replacement of unit is often wiser.

title: High Pressure Switch Fault
shortDescription: The high pressure switch circuit is abnormal.
fullDescription:
Error H3 indicates an abnormality in the high-pressure switch circuit. Either the switch has tripped (excessive high-side pressure) or the circuit is open due to a disconnected plug.

Causes of true high pressure include dirty outdoor coil, refrigerant overcharge, or failed outdoor fan.
safetyWarning: High-pressure refrigerant. EPA 608 required.

faq.a: For R-410A typically above ~580 PSI triggers.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Signal Error
shortDescription: Feedback signal from outdoor fan motor is abnormal.
fullDescription:
Error H7 indicates the outdoor fan motor position or speed feedback signal is out of expected range. Causes include a failed Hall sensor wire, seized bearing, or a damaged fan driver IC on the PCB.

Visually inspect and spin the fan by hand first.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power before touching fan.

faq.a: Similar symptoms; H7 is signal-side, E7 is broader motor fault.

title: Compressor DC Input Current Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The DC bus current sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
Error H8 indicates the DC current sensor in the outdoor inverter circuit is reporting an abnormal value. This sensor is essential for closed-loop control of the compressor and for overload protection.

PCB replacement is usually required.
safetyWarning: Lethal DC bus voltages present. Wait 10 minutes after power off.

causes.cause: DC current sensor failure on PCB

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCB for damage
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burnt shunt or sensor IC.

faq.a: Not economical; board-level replacement is standard.

title: Compressor Overcurrent (Instantaneous)
shortDescription: The compressor drew an instantaneous overcurrent.
fullDescription:
Error L2 indicates an instantaneous overcurrent event on the compressor phase. Different from L5 which is the inverter bus, L2 is measured on the AC side.

Causes include short cycling, refrigerant issues, or a failing compressor.
safetyWarning: Lethal voltages. Let capacitors discharge.

causes.cause: Short cycling due to thermostat issue

faq.a: Yes - shortens compressor life significantly.

title: Inverter Heat Sink Overheat
shortDescription: The inverter heat sink temperature sensor has exceeded its limit.
fullDescription:
Error L4 indicates the inverter heat sink has reached a critical temperature. Thermal paste degradation between the IPM and heat sink, or a failed heat sink fan, are common causes.

Professional service is typically needed to reseat the IPM with fresh thermal compound or replace the PCB assembly.
safetyWarning: Hot surfaces and lethal voltages.

causes.cause: Dried thermal paste between IPM and heat sink

fixSteps.title: Check cooling fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify auxiliary heat sink fan operates.

fixSteps.title: Reapply thermal paste
fixSteps.instruction: Pro to disassemble IPM and apply fresh compound.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for thermal paste replacement or IPM issues.

faq.q: How often should thermal paste be replaced?
faq.a: Typically lasts 7-10 years under normal conditions.

title: Power Supply Voltage Imbalance
shortDescription: Inverter detected power supply voltage imbalance or phase loss.
fullDescription:
Error P1 indicates the outdoor inverter detected power supply issues, most commonly voltage imbalance on 3-phase units or low/high voltage on single-phase units.

Verify line voltage with a multimeter before deeper diagnostics.
safetyWarning: High voltage measurements. Use proper PPE.
whenToCallPro: Utility voltage issues need electrician or utility.

faq.a: Yes - install surge protection with low-voltage cutoff.

title: Inverter Heat Sink Thermistor Fault
shortDescription: The heat sink temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Error P4 indicates the heat sink thermistor that monitors inverter module temperature is reporting an invalid value. Without this sensor, the system cannot safely operate the inverter.

The thermistor is typically integrated with or mounted on the outdoor PCB heat sink and may not be individually replaceable; PCB replacement is common.
safetyWarning: Lethal voltages on inverter PCB.

faq.q: Can I replace the thermistor alone?
faq.a: Sometimes; depends on model.

title: IGBT / IPM Abnormality
shortDescription: The IGBT or IPM on the outdoor inverter has faulted.
fullDescription:
Error P6 indicates an IGBT (insulated-gate bipolar transistor) or IPM fault on the outdoor inverter. These are the main switching devices that drive the compressor.

Replacement of the inverter PCB is typically required.
safetyWarning: Lethal voltages. Professional service only.

fixSteps.title: Professional diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Test IGBT with diode function on meter.

faq.a: Theoretically possible but rarely done vs full PCB swap.

title: Low Refrigerant / Insufficient Gas
shortDescription: Refrigerant charge is low, triggering gas shortage protection.
fullDescription:
Error U0 indicates the system detects insufficient refrigerant charge based on superheat/subcool calculations. A refrigerant leak is the usual cause and must be located and repaired before recharging.

Simply topping off refrigerant without finding the leak is illegal under EPA rules and will fail again. R-410A requires proper recovery and recharge procedures.
safetyWarning: R-410A is under high pressure. EPA 608 certification required.

fixSteps.title: Check service valves
fixSteps.instruction: Verify both service valves are fully open (counterclockwise).

fixSteps.title: Leak search
fixSteps.instruction: Pro uses electronic leak detector or soap bubbles on flares.

fixSteps.title: Repair leak
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten flares or replace damaged line.

fixSteps.title: Evacuate and recharge
fixSteps.instruction: Pull vacuum and weigh in correct charge per nameplate.

whenToCallPro: Always professional for leak repair and recharge.

faq.a: No. EPA 608 certification is required by law.

title: Reverse Phase / Phase Loss
shortDescription: Power supply phasing is reversed or a phase is missing.
fullDescription:
Error U1 indicates the outdoor unit has detected reverse phase or phase loss on its 3-phase input. Compressor rotation direction is critical, so the unit refuses to start.

Swap any two L1/L2/L3 conductors at the outdoor disconnect to correct phasing. Verify all three phases are present.
safetyWarning: High voltage wiring. Licensed electrician recommended.

fixSteps.title: Swap phases
fixSteps.instruction: If reversed, swap any two phase conductors at disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuses
fixSteps.instruction: If blown, replace with matching rating.

faq.a: Rare - single-phase models typically show different codes.

title: DC Bus Voltage Abnormal
shortDescription: DC bus voltage on the inverter is high or low.
fullDescription:
Error U2 indicates the DC bus voltage on the outdoor inverter is outside the safe operating window. Causes include low line voltage, failed rectifier, or a damaged DC bus capacitor.

PCB-level diagnosis is required.
safetyWarning: Lethal DC voltages. 10-minute discharge wait.

faq.a: Rural/far-end-of-line installs are more prone to U2.

title: Indoor-Outdoor Communication Error
shortDescription: Data cannot be exchanged between indoor and outdoor units.
fullDescription:
Error U4 indicates communication failure on the S1/S2/S3 signal line between indoor and outdoor units. Causes include broken wires, reversed polarity, water-damaged terminals, or PCB failure on either end.

Check wiring continuity and terminal tightness first. Many U4 faults resolve with proper wire termination.
safetyWarning: Disconnect both indoor and outdoor power before servicing terminals.

fixSteps.title: Inspect terminal block
fixSteps.instruction: Verify each S1/S2/S3 wire is tight at both indoor and outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Test continuity
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, verify end-to-end continuity of each wire.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if wiring looks intact but fault persists.

faq.a: Power and communication between indoor and outdoor units.
